newsitem.title: USA: Conrail reiterates desire to merge with CSX. [corrected 00:38 gmt 7/11]
newsitem.headline: Conrail reiterates desire to merge with CSX. [corrected 00:38 gmt 7/11]

text.p: Conrail Inc. Wednesday reiterated its desire to merge with CSX Corp. after CSX slightly sweetened the cash portion of its $8.4 billion bid for the railroad, which is also being pursued by Norfolk Southern Corp.
Conrail said its board had considered the merits of the rival bids and reaffirmed that a merger with CSX was a superior strategic combination, despite a higher cash offer by Norfolk Southern.
The merging of CSX and Conrail would create one of the largest transportation companies in the world, including a rail system with some 29,000 miles (47,000 km) of routes in 22 eastern states.
Some Conrail stockholders, however, expressed opposition to the company's acceptance of the CSX offer, which totals about $8.36 billion.

Norfolk Southern, meanwhile, issued a terse statement reaffirming its $100-a-share all-cash offer, which amounts to about $9.1 billion. It also said it had terminated its discussions with CSX (corrects from Conrail to CSX).
CSX said in a joint statement with Conrail that it raised the cash portion of its offer to $110 for each Conrail share from $92.50.

Under the revised CSX offer, the Richmond, Va.-based railroad would pay $4.01 billion for 40 percent of Conrail's 91 million outstanding shares. It would also offer 1.85619 of a CSX share, or about $4.358 billion based on Wednesday's trading price of $43, for the remaining shares.

That would value Philadelphia-based Conrail's shares at about $91.91 each, less than the $100 in cash that Norfolk Southern is offering. Conrail's stock gained $1.25 to $93.50 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Some Conrail stockholders expressed opposition to the deal in a company conference call with investors and Wall Street analysts.
"Some of the shareholders were really angry and said this was being crammed down their throats," said one expert on takeovers who listened to the conference call.
Other sources who participated in the call said several investors threatened to tender their shares for $110 and then vote against the proposed merger.
"It's an outrage. This thing is now locked up tighter than ever," said another participant.

In addition to the price of the CSX deal, investors were also unhappy with a three-month extension of the time in which Conrail is locked into the deal. The revised pact says Conrail cannot withdraw from the pact or agree to a competing transaction before July 12.

"It is clear to me that CSX and Conrail intend to continue their joint efforts to railroad Conrail shareholders into accepting a proposal significantly inferior to Norfolk Southern's $100 per share all cash tender offer," Norfolk Southern Charman David Goode said in a statement.

"Until CSX acknowledges that all Conrail shareholders are entitled to the $100 cash that they can only receive from Norfolk Southern's offer, any discussions between us are a waste of time," Goode added.

CSX Chairman John Snow said in the statement that the company's decision to raise its cash offer followed an analysis that identified at least $730 million in synergies and cost savings in a CSX-Conrail combination -- $180 million more than originally anticipated.
"Clearly, the combination of CSX and Conrail provides the best overall package of benefits to our constituencies, including customers, the communities we serve, and the public-at-large," Snow said.
"We welcome the strong support of the Conrail board of directors and look forward to a bright future as our new company moves full speed into the 21st century."
Snow also said that the Norfolk Southern bid was burdened with a number of conditions that would force Conrail shareholders to wait a prolonged amount of time to receive payment for their shares.
Norfolk Southern disputed that contention, however, saying that its offer included setting up a trust that would provide immediate cash payment to all shareholders.
The CSX-Conrail announcement also said that a Conrail shareholders' meeting scheduled for Nov. 14 had been cancelled, with a new meeting meeting expected to be held in mid-December.
It also said that, under the amended terms, CSX's tender offer's expiration date and withdrawal and proration rights were extended until midnight Nov. 20.
